response.rationale: The vignette describes a child with asymmetric facial movement specifically affecting the lower lip during smiling or crying, while the rest of the face is symmetric. This is the defining characteristic of Asymmetric crying face syndrome. Candidate D4, Congenital unilateral hypoplasia of the depressor anguli oris muscle, is a specific cause of this syndrome, but D1 is the broader, more direct diagnosis based on the presented symptoms. D2 is contradicted by the normal neurodevelopmental exam, and D3 is too general.
